data.title: Coda Octopus Earnings Call Highlights Defense‑Led Growth
data.description:
Coda Octopus Group ((CODA)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Coda Octopus Group’s latest earnings call carried a broadly upbeat tone, as management highlighted solid revenue and pretax income growth, strong contributions from defense engineering services and acoustic sensors, and a debt‑free balance sheet with $31.7 million in cash. The optimism was tempered by softer marine technology revenue, lower gross margins, and reminders that defense procurement remains lumpy and slow‑burn by nature.

Consolidated Growth Driven by Defense and Acoustics

Third‑quarter fiscal 2026 consolidated revenue rose 9.2% to $7.7 million from $7.1 million, while pretax income climbed 16% to $1.8 million from $1.5 million. Management said robust defense engineering services and acoustic sensors and materials more than offset a 15.2% slide in marine technology revenue.

Promotion

  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Defense Engineering Services Surge on Program Activity

Defense engineering services revenue jumped 68.3% to $2.7 million from $1.6 million, fueled by increased activity and funding across long‑standing defense programs. The U.K. defense operations posted higher revenue, and the U.S. business saw stronger demand for repairs and spares, pointing to deepening customer engagement.

Sustainment Contracts and Spares Orders Add Visibility

A prime contractor secured a multiyear repair and sustainment contract from the U.S. government, triggering more repair work and new subcontract opportunities for Coda. Spares orders tied to these sustainment systems have already exceeded $2.4 million year to date, supporting recurring revenue streams.

Push into Electronic Warfare and Next‑Gen Defense Systems

The U.S. defense engineering arm is now helping several prime contractors develop rugged RF electronic warfare systems for unmanned systems, helicopters, airborne pods, and ground vehicles. Management said Coda is collaborating with no fewer than four prime defense contractors, expanding beyond legacy programs into emerging defense technology.

Acoustic Sensors and Materials Show Steady Demand

Acoustic sensors and materials revenue grew 10.4% to $1.6 million from $1.5 million, underscoring resilient demand despite regional disruptions. Management cited encouraging orders for acoustic materials and acoustic test tank solutions across international markets as key contributors.

Rental Strength Lifts Marine Technology Margins

While marine technology revenue declined overall, rental revenue soared 131.1% to roughly $700,000 from about $300,000. This shift toward rentals, along with lower commission costs from changing sales geography, pushed marine technology gross margin up to 78.5% from 77%.

Navy Authorization Paves Way for DAVID Deployment

The U.S. Navy completed its authorization for Navy‑use assessment of the DAVID untethered system featuring the Gen 4 HUD, removing a key gate to broader deployment. Coda has now delivered 24 DAVID untethered systems, including 16 earlier this year, allowing operational commands to fully evaluate and utilize the technology.

New DAVID Orders and Training Integration Momentum

Since the previous call, Coda secured about $1.4 million of U.S. Navy orders for DAVID tethered systems and peripherals, including four DAVID Flex units and Echoscope sonars for training. Management noted growing institutional acceptance in the naval diving community and the potential inclusion of DAVID in diving school and academy curricula.

European Navy Interest Could Catalyze Wider Adoption

The company continues to work closely with a European Navy that recently purchased DAVID systems and remains highly engaged. Management expects more clarity on that customer’s procurement roadmap later in the year, and believes broader adoption by this influential navy could prompt other European navies to follow and spur pull‑through sales of Echoscope and port inspection systems.

Defense Programs Advancing DAVID and Nano Use Cases

Several funded defense programs are now integrating DAVID and Nano technologies into diver‑machine teaming concepts and diver health‑state monitoring. These initiatives also explore advanced deep‑saturation diving applications, providing Coda with real‑world environments to showcase and refine its technologies.

NanoGen Sonar Gains Early Market Traction

Coda reported a positive early reception for its NanoGen series, an ultra‑compact real‑time 3D sonar aimed at small subsea robotics and AI‑enabled autonomous underwater platforms. The firm is working with subsea robotic OEMs, research organizations, and direct customers worldwide, with growing interest from U.S. and European defense markets and various underwater systems.

ROV OEM Program Approaches Critical SAT Trials

An underwater ROV OEM that purchased Echoscope and NanoGen units for testing has moved its program to imminent SAT trials, with vehicles already active in the water. The initial order covers three systems on the vehicle, and management sees additional customer opportunities if these trials deliver strong results.

Strategic Investment in Next‑Gen Tech and VoiceHub 4

Coda is ramping up R&D and SG&A to broaden the number of defense programs adopting its technology portfolio, including leveraging PAL’s acoustics capabilities. The company is also future‑proofing Echoscope for more underwater platforms and advancing VoiceHub 4 after redesigning it to lower bill‑of‑materials costs.

Improved Profitability Metrics Despite Margin Pressure

Gross profit increased to $5.1 million from $4.8 million, while operating income edged up to $1.5 million from $1.4 million, lifting operating margin to 19.9% from 19.5%. Net income rose to $1.4 million, or $0.12 per diluted share, compared with $1.3 million, or $0.11 per diluted share, showing disciplined cost control.

SG&A Efficiency Supports Earnings Performance

Selling, general, and administrative expenses fell slightly to $2.8 million from $2.9 million, helped by lower payroll costs and favorable foreign‑exchange impacts. As a share of revenue, SG&A dropped to 36.1% from 40.6%, partially offset by higher contingent consideration tied to the PAL earnout.

Debt‑Free Balance Sheet Underpins Strategic Flexibility

As of July 31, 2026, Coda held $31.7 million in cash and cash equivalents and remained entirely debt free, with total assets of $68.9 million versus $64.5 million at October 31, 2025. Management emphasized that this strong liquidity profile gives the company ample room to pursue organic growth and selective strategic initiatives.

Retained Earnings Milestone and Active M&A Pipeline

The company moved from an accumulated deficit to positive retained earnings for the first time, reflecting sustained profitability and financial discipline. Coda also remains actively engaged in evaluating acquisitions that fit its strategic goals, hinting at potential deal‑driven expansion.

Marine Technology Hit by Geopolitics and Hardware Drop

Marine technology revenue fell 15.2% to $3.4 million from $4.0 million, mainly due to geopolitical instability in the Middle East and parts of Asia limiting customer activity. Within that segment, hardware revenue declined 17.8% to $2.3 million from $2.7 million, underscoring the impact of regional disruptions.

Deferral of Marine Opportunities Amid Regional Uncertainty

Management said ongoing uncertainty has caused security concerns, offshore project disruptions, and supply‑chain issues for end customers in affected regions. While these factors are leading to deferred orders, the company does not believe the situation reflects structural weakness in the underlying marine technology market.

Compressed Consolidated and Segment Margins

Consolidated gross margin slipped to 65.4% from 68.3%, driven by shifts in revenue composition, geography, and project mix. Acoustic sensors and materials margins eased to 52.4% from 54.8%, while defense engineering services margins fell to 56.9% from 58.9%, both reflecting contract and product mix dynamics.

Defense Revenue Remains Lumpy and Long Cycle

Management cautioned that defense engineering revenue will stay lumpy because sustainment spending depends on annual program budgets and timing of spare‑parts replenishment. They stressed that DAVID, Nano, and related defense opportunities are inherently long‑term, with broader procurement hinging on deployment, user testing, and complex customer processes.

Operating Expenses and Taxes Edge Higher

Total operating expenses rose to $3.5 million from $3.4 million, reflecting greater investment to support growth, while the income tax provision increased to $400,000 from $300,000. Even with these higher charges, Coda maintained year‑over‑year gains in operating income and net earnings.

Forward‑Looking Outlook and Program Milestones

Looking ahead, management expects marine technology activity in Asia and the Middle East to remain affected by deferred opportunities but views this as temporary rather than structural. Defense sustainment revenue will stay uneven, SAT trials for an underwater ROV program are expected to conclude in the fourth quarter, visibility into a European Navy’s procurement roadmap should improve later this fiscal year, and R&D and SG&A spending are set to increase as Coda pursues longer‑term defense programs.

Coda Octopus Group’s earnings call painted a picture of a company leaning into growth in defense and acoustic technologies while absorbing near‑term marine market headwinds and margin pressure. For investors, the combination of rising profitability, a debt‑free balance sheet, and a growing portfolio of longer‑cycle defense programs suggests a business with solid resilience and meaningful optionality, even if revenue streams remain uneven from quarter to quarter.

data.title: SeSa S.p.A. Earnings Call Signals Confident Outlook
data.description:
Sesa S.p.A. ((IT:SES)) has held its Q1 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

SeSa’s latest earnings call struck an upbeat note, with management highlighting fully organic growth in revenue and EBITDA and solid momentum across key value-added segments. Despite a soft patch in Software and System Integration and lingering higher interest costs, executives expressed confidence that the group’s diversified model, strong cash generation and disciplined capital allocation will support sustained value creation.

Solid Organic Revenue and EBITDA Growth

First-quarter consolidated revenue and other income rose to EUR 900 million, up 6.5% year-on-year, with all growth coming organically. EBITDA climbed 7.6% to EUR 65 million and the margin nudged higher to 7.23%, signaling that SeSa is not only expanding its top line but also improving efficiency and profitability at the group level.

Promotion

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks

Continued Investment in Skills, AI and Efficiency

Management stressed ongoing investment in skills, AI, automation and operating efficiency as the backbone of its scalable organic growth strategy. These initiatives support execution of the FY 2027-2028 industrial plan, aiming to deepen capabilities in high-demand digital areas while keeping the cost base lean and adaptable to evolving market dynamics.

ICT VAS Maintains Strong Momentum

ICT Value-Added Services remained a growth engine, with revenue reaching EUR 540 million, up 8.1% and fully organic. Demand is being driven by data management, data sovereignty and cybersecurity solutions that underpin private AI and automation, positioning SeSa squarely in the core of Italy’s digital transformation.

ICT VAS Profitability on the Rise

Profitability in ICT VAS improved alongside growth, as EBITDA rose 11% year-on-year to EUR 25 million. The EBITDA margin ticked up to 4.6% from 4.5%, showing that SeSa can convert rising demand for advanced digital services into better earnings, not just higher revenues.

Green VAS Delivers Double-Digit Growth

Green VAS extended its strong run, with revenue climbing 14.4% year-on-year to EUR 127 million, continuing the double-digit organic trend seen in FY 2026. Management linked this performance to increasing energy demand from digitalization, especially the rapid expansion of the data center market, which requires efficient energy solutions.

Green VAS Margin Expansion

EBITDA in Green VAS jumped 23% to EUR 7.7 million, lifting the EBITDA margin to 6.0% from 5.6%. Synergies from the merger of PM Service and GreenSun were cited as a key driver, and management believes the 6% margin is sustainable, offering investors a mix of high growth and improving profitability in this segment.

Business Services Returns to Double-Digit Growth

Business Services posted a clear turnaround, with revenue rising 11% to EUR 41 million and confirming the expected return to double-digit organic growth in FY 2027. The rebound is fueled by multiyear contracts won in FY 2026 and a stronger focus on digital platforms and vertical applications for clients.

Business Services Profitability Improvement

EBITDA in Business Services increased 18% year-on-year to EUR 8.6 million, pushing the margin up to 21% from 19.9%. Management expects to at least maintain this level and potentially improve quarter by quarter as more revenue flows through the same platforms and applications, enhancing operating leverage.

Software and System Integration Efficiency Despite Revenue Dip

Software and System Integration revenue slipped about 3% year-on-year to EUR 230 million, reflecting disposals of nonstrategic assets and ongoing organizational reengineering. Still, EBITDA margin in the segment edged up to 10.8% from 10.7%, signaling that efficiency measures are working even as the business resets.

Software and System Integration Profitability Trends

EBITDA in Software and System Integration declined 2.5% to EUR 23 million and reported adjusted EAT dipped 1%, though excluding asset disposals, EBITDA was flat and adjusted EAT grew 1%. Management expects this segment to return to revenue growth from Q2 FY 2027, particularly in higher-value technology and integration services.

Growth in Adjusted and Reported Earnings

At group level, adjusted EBIT reached EUR 50.2 million, up 6.2% year-on-year, while reported EBIT climbed 7.5% to EUR 41.4 million. Adjusted EAT rose 7.1% to EUR 30.1 million, underpinned by strong profitability in ICT VAS, Green VAS and Business Services, reinforcing the earnings power of SeSa’s diversified portfolio.

Net Financial Expenses and Cost of Capital

Net financial expenses were around EUR 7.5 million, improving 11% versus the fourth quarter of FY 2026 and in line with the industrial plan assumptions. However, they were slightly higher than a year earlier, highlighting that SeSa is still partly exposed to elevated interest rates and a higher cost of capital environment.

Strong Cash Generation and Financial Position

Reported net financial position as of July 2026 showed EUR 23.4 million of net debt, an improvement of about EUR 40 million year-on-year despite EUR 120 million of investments and EUR 40 million returned via dividends and buybacks. Excluding IFRS liabilities, SeSa held around EUR 150 million of net cash, slightly better than a year before.

Consistent Operating and Free Cash Flow

Management highlighted that operating cash flow over the last 12 months was about EUR 200 million for the fourth consecutive quarter. Free cash flow over the same period reached roughly EUR 80 million, underscoring SeSa’s ability to fund growth, shareholder returns and acquisitions without stretching its balance sheet.

Sustainability and Information Security Progress

SeSa reaffirmed its key ESG ratings, including EcoVadis Platinum, MSCI BBB and CDP Level B, and completed ISO 27001 certification across main group companies in FY 2026. The group continues to extend certifications and increase renewable energy use, integrating sustainability and information security into its long-term strategy.

Stable Workforce and Focus on High-Demand Skills

The workforce remained stable at around 6,700–6,770 people, up roughly 2.5% to 2.7% year-on-year but flat versus April 2026. Management tied this stability to initiatives around skills development, knowledge sharing, AI and automation, efficiency, education, welfare, inclusion and work-life balance, aimed at keeping talent aligned with growth areas.

Higher Dividend and Share Buyback Programs

The new industrial plan confirms a payout ratio of about 40%, and the dividend to be paid in late September will rise from EUR 1 to EUR 1.33 per share. Management sees potential to reach up to EUR 2 per share over the next two years, alongside a EUR 5 million buyback, an additional EUR 5 million program and possible further purchases within a broader authorization.

Positive Market and Order Environment

Management described the Italian digital market as supportive, with expected growth of around 3.5% per year through 2029 driven by AI, cloud, cybersecurity and data management. SeSa continues to grow at roughly twice the market rate and reported a positive order trend, strong ICT VAS momentum and an anticipated recovery in Software and System Integration.

Simplified Holding Structure and Ownership Increase

The merger of two holding entities into the new SeSa Holding was presented as a strategic simplification that clarifies SeSa Holding as the group’s long-term owner. SeSa Holding’s stake has risen to about 57.1% from 52.8% 18 months ago, and management intends to continue increasing its ownership over time.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Outlook

Looking ahead to FY 2027, SeSa confirmed guidance for revenue growth of 5% to 7.5%, targeting EUR 3.8 billion to EUR 3.9 billion. EBITDA is expected to grow 5% to 10% to EUR 274 million–287 million, with adjusted group EAT seen rising 7.5% to 12.5% to EUR 115 million–119 million, driven by continued outperformance versus the Italian digital market.

SeSa anticipates Software and System Integration returning to low single-digit growth in revenue and profitability from Q2 2027, with Business Services aiming to maintain or improve its strong EBITDA margin quarter by quarter. Green VAS is expected to sustain a 6% EBITDA margin and about 3.5% net profitability, while the company plans to keep growing at roughly twice the national digital market rate.

Overall, the earnings call painted a picture of a company balancing growth, profitability and shareholder returns while navigating pockets of softness and higher financing costs. For investors, the key takeaways are SeSa’s resilient cash generation, accelerating value-added segments and unchanged—but potentially upgradeable—guidance, all underpinned by a long-term digital and sustainability strategy.

data.title: Rf Industries Signals Momentum With Record Earnings Call
data.description:
Rf Industries, Ltd. ((RFIL)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Rf Industries, Ltd. delivered a notably upbeat earnings call, highlighting record revenue, rising profitability, and stronger margins across the business. Management acknowledged some pockets of softness and timing-related hurdles, but emphasized broad demand, improving cash generation, and growing confidence that momentum will carry into the fourth quarter and beyond.

Record Revenue Sets New Benchmark

Third-quarter revenue reached a record $24 million, rising 21% year over year and 16% sequentially. Management framed the performance as a new high watermark for RF Industries, reinforcing the narrative that its strategic repositioning toward higher-value solutions is translating into tangible top-line growth.

Promotion

  • Unlock powerful investing tools with TipRanks Premium to make smarter, more confident investment decisions
  • Subscribe to TipRanks Smart Investor Newsletter, and discover new investing opportunities with data-backed stock picks
Learn more about TipRanks Premium

Margin Expansion and Gross Profit Strength

Gross profit climbed 27% to $8.5 million, while gross margin expanded 160 basis points to 35.6% from 34%. Executives noted they have exceeded their 30% gross-margin objective in six of the last seven quarters, signaling disciplined pricing, better mix, and operational efficiency.

Operating Income and Profitability Upshift

Operating income surged to $1.8 million from $720,000 a year earlier, pushing operating margin to 7.3% from 3.6%. The sharp improvement underscores how higher volumes and richer product mix are flowing through the P&L, giving the company more earnings power even in a mixed spending environment.

Net Income and EPS Move Higher

Consolidated net income rose to $1.4 million, or $0.12 per diluted share, versus $392,000, or $0.04 per share, in the prior-year quarter. On a non-GAAP basis, net income advanced to $2.2 million, or $0.19 per share, from $1.1 million, or $0.10, reflecting underlying profit growth beyond accounting adjustments.

Adjusted EBITDA Above Long-Term Target

Adjusted EBITDA jumped about 71% to $2.7 million from $1.6 million, with margin improving to 11.1% from 7.9%. Management highlighted that this level is above its 10% long-term EBITDA goal, suggesting the business model is scaling efficiently and offering room for reinvestment.

Year-to-Date Growth Shows Consistency

For the first nine months, sales increased 10% to $63.6 million and gross profit rose 19% to $21.9 million. Gross margin expanded to 34.5% from 31.8%, while operating income grew to $3 million from $882,000 and adjusted EBITDA climbed 61% to $5.7 million, underscoring sustained, multi-quarter progress.

Liquidity and Net Debt Improvement

As of July 31, 2026, RF Industries held $4.5 million in cash, $18.3 million of working capital, and a current ratio near 2.0. Cash increased by about $1.1 million in the quarter and revolver borrowings fell by roughly $400,000 to $5.7 million, leading management to describe a meaningful improvement in net debt.

Demand, Bookings, and Backlog Support Outlook

Third-quarter bookings were $22.5 million following a record second quarter, and year-to-date bookings remained ahead of sales. Backlog rose from $18.6 million at quarter-end to $19.8 million as of the call, with management saying the backlog and opportunity pipeline offer a solid foundation heading into the final quarter.

Balanced Segment Contributions

Every segment contributed meaningfully, with custom cabling continuing to lead the way. Interconnect stepped up from the second quarter, while integrated systems gained traction, and management emphasized that contribution across the portfolio is becoming more balanced, reducing reliance on any single product line.

Diversification Across End Markets

The company’s solutions now reach aerospace, edge data centers, AI infrastructure, industrial manufacturing, medical imaging, transportation, and public safety. Third-quarter results were fueled by aerospace and defense, telecom, industrial, and distribution customers, with new contributors emerging across these markets.

Higher-Value Solutions Drive Growth

Higher-value integrated systems and custom cabling solutions gained momentum and made a significant impact on Q3 performance. Management stressed that these offerings carry more engineering content, cover larger project scopes, and deepen customer relationships, enhancing both revenue quality and stickiness.

Integrated Engineering and Product Management

RF Industries unified its engineering and product line management functions under a single structure within interconnect and integrated systems. The change aims to accelerate product launches, sharpen accountability, and strengthen execution on complex programs, ultimately improving solutions delivered to customers.

Operational Execution and Supply Chain Flexibility

Management said operations were “firing on all cylinders,” citing a U.S.-based manufacturing footprint and a deliberately diverse supply chain. This setup is meant to provide flexibility to respond to shifting demand patterns and navigate evolving tariff and geopolitical dynamics without major disruption.

AI as a Business Enablement Tool

The company is expanding use of AI in sales and customer-facing roles to help teams work smarter and respond faster. The roadmap calls for extending AI into engineering, operations, and supply chain in coming quarters, positioning RF Industries to leverage data and automation for competitive advantage.

Fourth-Quarter Revenue Outlook

With one quarter left, management reaffirmed its expectation for a strong second half. Based on current visibility, fiscal fourth-quarter sales are projected to be roughly in line with or above the Q3 level of $24 million, reflecting sustained demand despite some pockets of timing-related softness.

Scaling DAC Business

The DAC business, once immaterial, now generates millions of dollars per quarter and is expected to exceed $10 million in sales and accelerate further. Opportunities are expanding beyond traditional telecom and wireless markets into adjacent sectors, broadening the growth runway.

Aerospace Strength and Expansion

Management described its relationship with a large aerospace customer as strong, underpinned by design, engineering, and technical work from the Long Island team. Experience from that engagement is helping RF Industries open doors and advance discussions with additional aerospace customers.

Edge Data Center and Cooling Opportunities

Deployments at the edge of the network are accelerating, and RF Industries is participating in more customer conversations. Management highlighted that, in some situations, edge deployments can be 70% to 80% more cost effective than large data centers due to lower water and electricity needs, creating an attractive niche.

Small Cell Recovery, NEMA 4 Timing

The small cell market remained challenging, with deployments and technology factors delaying expected revenue earlier in the year. Dollars delivered were behind plan, but the business gained momentum in Q3 and is expected to accelerate into Q4 and fiscal 2027, while NEMA 4 and related wireline opportunities should become more material next year.

Bookings, Carrier Spending, and Order Timing

Third-quarter bookings of $22.5 million trailed revenue, producing a book-to-bill ratio of about 0.94, though management noted backlog can swing with order timing and fulfillment. Wireless carrier capital spending is projected to be largely flat, and aerospace orders may vary quarter to quarter as inventory levels and shipment schedules move.

Forward-Looking Guidance and Balance Sheet Goals

Management expects fiscal fourth-quarter sales to be roughly level with or above the $24 million posted in Q3. It sees the small cell market gaining traction into next year, DAC sales surpassing $10 million, and NEMA 4 and edge-related deployments accelerating into fiscal 2027, while targeting further net debt reduction to a level seen as immaterial relative to the balance sheet.

RF Industries’ earnings call painted a picture of a company executing well on growth and margin expansion while navigating uneven telecom spending and project timing. For investors, the mix of record results, rising cash, diversified demand, and measured but confident guidance suggests a business building resilience and optionality across multiple high-value markets.

data.title: Enova Ends Bank Bid, Boosts Share Repurchase Plans
data.description:
Enova International ( (ENVA) ) has provided an announcement.
